name: Sir Kay
one_line: Arthur's foster-brother and steward: a giant-killing hero in Welsh, and a sour-tongued fool in French.

aka.note: in Culhwch, a hero with supernatural gifts

dossier:
In the Welsh **Culhwch and Olwen**, Cai is formidable: he can go nine nights without sleep, hold his breath nine days underwater, make himself as tall as a tree, and no physician can heal a wound from his sword. He is one of the great warriors of Arthur's band.

By the time French romance is done with him he is the seneschal — the household steward — and the court's designated bad-tempered fool: quick with an insult, quick to volunteer, and reliably unhorsed within a page. Every romance needs someone to be wrong first so the hero can be right, and Kay drew the job.

Malory keeps the French Kay but remembers the older one at the edges. He is the reason the sword comes out of the stone at all: he forgets his own sword at the tournament, sends his young foster-brother back for it, and briefly claims the one the boy returns with. And he is loyal to the end, dying with Arthur's household.
